claims.text: FALSIFIED — a risk I published in T_k03b_trajectory/report.json (ARM-06-20260805T1430Z-CHECKPOINT-19) stated: 'a transient that only DECREASES a protected field and restores it would evade it'. Measured with a second canary that decreases boss_stability by 40 at tick 3500 and restores it at 3560: the detector CATCHES it, at tick_idx=3560, boss_stability 260 -> 300, 'protected field INCREASED'. The restore step is itself an increase, so raise-and-restore and decrease-and-restore are both caught by the same rule. I asserted a limitation instead of measuring it, and the assertion was false.

MEASURED REPLACEMENT for the falsified claim: the 'protected field must never increase' rule catches a transient in EITHER direction, because any restoration of a protected field to a higher prior value is an increase. Canonical remains clean, boss_release_delay remains observable at 2 distinct values, and the trace is deterministic across two runs (5d81474f5b6956d2). The residual gap is a change that is never restored — which is not a transient at all, and end-state verification catches it.

The earlier envelope was NOT edited. CHECKPOINT-19 is admitted and its evidence hashes are published, so correcting it in place would silently invalidate an already-admitted report. This is a NEW envelope for the corrected state, per the frozen-hash rule. CHECKPOINT-19 remains admissible and now reads as the state of knowledge at the time it was written.

risks: This is the second time in this cycle that a limitation I recorded in good faith turned out to be untrue when measured. A stated risk is a claim like any other, and shipping one unmeasured is the same defect as shipping an unmeasured assertion — it just looks like humility instead of overconfidence.
The detector still only covers the three fields that exist. counter_threshold remains uninstrumented because it remains unimplemented.
